The grand tourer,
veiled in silk.

Scroll slowly. The cover slips away and the car steps into the light.

Every line,
drawn once.

One long flank in deep burgundy lacquer, with chrome that catches every beam.

The
stance.

Low, long and unhurried. Ready to cross a continent.

Hand-cut
glass.

A fluted lens behind a polished chrome bezel.

The
face.

A woven chrome grille and sculpted bumper guards.

Wire
wheels.

Polished spokes laced around a hub of brass.

A quilted
cabin.

Tan leather, burr walnut and a wood-rimmed wheel.

The last
word.

Round lamps, twin pipes per side, and a chrome bumper.

Scroll

Built to be driven.
Sideways, in style.

Twelve coats of lacquer. A wood-rimmed wheel. And a rear end that never stays still for long.
